profile.reading: This H5 Data Centers facility is located at 1125 Energy Park Drive, Suite 100, St. Paul, Minnesota 55108, in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metro area. The building totals approximately 17,000 square feet, with N+1 UPS power, multiple diesel generators with 48 hour runtime, cold aisle containment, and N+1 CRAC cooling, per the operator own facility page. The facility connects to 6 on net carriers. No MW capacity figure is published for this specific building. A January 31, 2022 H5 Data Centers press release documents that this St. Paul, Minnesota facility was one of seven data centers, alongside sites in Nashville, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Portland, Secaucus, New Jersey, and St. Louis, that H5 acquired from vXchnge in a deal totaling more than 250,000 square feet of data center space and over 150 customers, expanding H5's portfolio to 20 markets at the time. The Secaucus, New Jersey facility acquired in that same deal is this registry's separate H5 Secaucus row. H5 Data Centers is a privately held US colocation and wholesale data center operator with facilities spanning roughly two dozen markets nationwide, per the company's own site. This St. Paul building sits in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metro's Energy Park area, a secondary but established Midwest data center market served by Xcel Energy, whose relatively low industrial electricity rates and access to regional wind generation have helped draw colocation and enterprise investment to Minnesota alongside larger operators like Involta and Cologix, whose Minneapolis area facilities are tracked elsewhere in this registry. H5 is not a publicly traded company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's specifications are sourced to the operator's own published facility page and its own acquisition press release rather than an independently audited source, a limitation this registry notes rather than treats as disqualifying, consistent with its general practice for privately held colocation operators. No MW capacity figure or year opened date was located for this specific building.

reading.body:
H5 Minneapolis occupies 17,000 square feet in Saint Paul's Energy Park district, which is served by Xcel Energy and benefits from regional wind generation and industrial electricity rates that have attracted colocation investment to the Minneapolis-St. Paul metro. The facility's total MW capacity is not published. No opening date is published, though H5 acquired this building from vXchnge in January 2022 as part of a portfolio expansion that added seven data centers across multiple Midwest and Northeast markets.

The campus is certified for SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS workloads, indicating compliance-grade security and audit readiness rather than specialization for any particular use case. It has N+1 UPS and cooling redundancy, multiple diesel generators with 48-hour runtime, cold aisle containment, and connections to six on-net carriers. These are standard colocation specifications without published evidence of AI-grade density, power delivery, or cooling infrastructure.

Minnesota has 13 mapped data center facilities in this registry and only 2 with published MW figures totaling 10 MW, placing H5 Minneapolis third by published capacity in the state. Without a published capacity figure for this specific 17,000-square-foot building, its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling cannot be determined from the available data. The facility operates as a regional colocation player in an established secondary Midwest market, not as a hyperscale or dedicated AI compute campus.
